sources.claim: "A registered report is a scholarly publishing format in which the research question, study design, and analysis plan are peer-reviewed before data are collected or analyzed." Stage 1 review is on the theoretical rationale, research question, design and analysis plan before data exist; Stage 2 review is the full manuscript with results after completion. The fetch reported one further sentence attributed to the article text: "In 2026, they expanded Registered Reports to additional research areas and to include both confirmatory and exploratory research," with no physics- or mathematics-specific sentence located.

Cited here only as continuing external precedent for Round33's own exact-arithmetic freeze rule (freeze_contract.py); it names no physics or mathematics field by name, so it supports the general trend, not a discipline-specific claim.

sources.title: Divine Contenders: Wolfgang Pauli and the Symmetry of the World
sources.author: F. David Peat
sources.version_date: Essay originally published in Psychological Perspectives, Spring-Summer 1988; hosted, undated, at the Pari Center for New Learning
sources.section: Passages on symmetry as archetype, the unus mundus, and Pauli's programme of a 'neutral language' spanning physics and psychology
sources.reading_depth: Fetched (tool-mediated; not a raw HTML download; quotations as returned by the fetch tool, attributed to specific sentences)
sources.provenance: Secondary essay by a physicist-historian (Peat), hosted by a Jung-affiliated study center; not a primary Pauli text
sources.claim: "Symmetry, for Pauli, was an archetype, the underlying ground out of which scientific descriptions of nature arise." "Rather than seeking the ultimate level of nature in terms of elementary particles, Pauli believed that the material level is the manifestation of something deeper, an unus mundus." Peat reports Pauli sought a duality "between synchronicity and causality as well as between energy and the space-time continuum", and a 'neutral language' for physics and psychology; and that "Mind and matter, emerging out of the unus mundus, contain the imprint of their origin ... the archetypes or abstract symmetries."
sources.historical_assertion: Pauli held that psyche and matter share a common, pre-differentiated origin (the unus mundus), of which causal, spatiotemporal physics and acausal, meaning-based synchronicity are two complementary readouts.
sources.physical_claim_status: None admitted. No premise, coupling, region or topology of any Round33 model is drawn from this reading. Used only as the documented historical shape of a causal/acausal explanatory-map pair -- directly relevant, as cultural context only, to Direction B's dynamics comparison (a strictly causal, finite-speed Lieb-Robinson bound) being read against the Round32-documented cautionary record of an acausal 'connecting principle' claimed without any such bound (Jung, Synchronicity, inherited).
sources.relevance: Supplies the observation-map contrast this memo section 1 uses under Direction B: a Lieb-Robinson/Duhamel bound is a finite-propagation-speed, causal comparison; Pauli/Jung's synchronicity is the documented historical case of an explicitly acausal claim advanced without any discriminating bound. The contrast sharpens why 'boundary independent' must always carry its window and region, never stand as a bare claim of an unconditioned, all-scales connection.
sources.unresolved: Peat's essay is a secondary, sympathetic account; it was not cross-read against a Pauli primary source this pass (the ETH Pauli Archive remains inaccessible, as in Round32 -- see reading-ledger.md). No claim here rests on Peat's characterization being historically complete.
